```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

## The cohesion RAV basis ships with the package as a compact subset, so
## inferpheno() runs out of the box. This held-out CMS example additionally
## needs two Suggests packages (the demo data and gene-ID mapping); when those
## are absent the chunks are shown but not evaluated, and the outputs printed
## below are the real results from one such run.
have_deps <- requireNamespace("CMScaller", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("org.Hs.eg.db", quietly = TRUE)

## The figures below need ggplot2 in addition to the live results; gate them
## separately so the numeric analysis still runs without a plotting backend.
have_plot <- have_deps && requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
```

# What this shows

`InferPheno` infers a phenotype from gene expression in two stages: it
**projects** new expression onto a fixed, unsupervised
[Replicable Axes of Variation (RAV)](https://bioconductor.org/packages/GenomicSuperSignature)
basis, then applies a small **supervised head** trained once and shipped
with the package. Because the feature basis is fixed before the label is
seen, a head can be applied to cohorts and platforms it never saw during
fitting.

This quick start does exactly that: it takes a head trained on **primary**
colorectal cancer (CRC) and uses it to call consensus molecular subtype
(CMS) on a **held-out, metastatic** CRC cohort profiled on a different
platform — none of whose samples were part of training.

# Setup

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install("~/GSS/InferPheno")
```

```{r libs, eval = have_deps}
library(InferPheno)
```

`inferpheno()` needs the RAV basis the heads were built on. A compact subset
of the cohesion basis — just the RAVs the shipped heads use — is bundled with
the package, so no setup is required. You only need the full ~190 MB basis to
develop or refit heads; point InferPheno at it to override the bundled subset
(see [the README](https://github.com/shbrief/InferPheno)):

```{r basis, eval = FALSE}
options(inferpheno.rav_model_path = "/path/to/RAVmodel_cohesion.rds")
# or  Sys.setenv(INFERPHENO_RAV_MODEL = "/path/to/RAVmodel_cohesion.rds")
# or  pass it directly:  inferpheno(expr, ..., rav_model = readRDS("..."))
```

## What can I infer today?

`availablePheno()` is the live contract: each row is a phenotype
`inferpheno()` can be called on, with the head's out-of-fold performance.

```{r avail, eval = have_deps}
availablePheno()
```

```{r avail-show, echo = FALSE, eval = !have_deps}
data.frame(
  phenotype = c("sex", "msi_status", "msi_score", "cms_subtype", "neutrophil"),
  kind      = c("binary", "binary", "regression", "multiclass", "regression"),
  n_train   = c(2069L, 745L, 555L, 1355L, 76L),
  metric    = c("auc_oof", "auc_oof", "r2_oof", "accuracy_oof", "r2_oof"),
  perf      = c(0.994, 0.951, 0.701, 0.714, 0.987))
```

# A held-out example: CMS on metastatic CRC

The `cms_subtype` head was trained across eight primary-CRC microarray
cohorts plus TCGA RNA-seq (n = 1,355). For a fair held-out test we use the
Oslo metastatic-CRC series shipped with
[CMScaller](https://bioconductor.org/packages/CMScaller)
(`mcrcOSLOsubset`, n = 295) — a different lab, platform, and disease stage,
absent from training. Its CMS calls from CMScaller's PAM classifier serve
as the reference.

```{r load-oslo, eval = have_deps}
library(InferPheno)
library(CMScaller)        # held-out data + reference CMS calls
library(Biobase)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)

data("mcrcOSLOsubset")
eset <- mcrcOSLOsubset
```

`inferpheno()` expects HGNC-symbol rownames, so map the cohort's Entrez IDs:

```{r prep, eval = have_deps}
expr <- exprs(eset)
sym  <- mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, rownames(expr),
               keytype = "ENTREZID", column = "SYMBOL", multiVals = "first")
keep <- !is.na(sym) & !duplicated(sym)
expr <- expr[keep, ]
rownames(expr) <- sym[keep]
dim(expr)        # genes x samples
```

```{r prep-show, echo = FALSE, eval = !have_deps}
cat("#> [1] 1373  295\n")
```

Now infer. Project the whole cohort at once (the projection standardizes
genes across the samples you pass, so give it a cohort, not one sample at a
time):

```{r infer, eval = have_deps}
res <- inferpheno(expr, "cms_subtype")
res[1:4, 1:5]
```

```{r infer-show, echo = FALSE, eval = !have_deps}
cat("#>        class         CMS1        CMS2        CMS3        CMS4\n",
    "#> 001_T1  CMS2 0.0004680278 0.781343300 0.005338214 0.212850458\n",
    "#> 002_T1  CMS2 0.0002105928 0.899164325 0.002530896 0.098094186\n",
    "#> 003_T1  CMS1 0.5186408226 0.001405632 0.478320248 0.001633298\n",
    "#> 003_T2  CMS1 0.7593658896 0.001902760 0.220010827 0.018720524\n",
    sep = "")
```

The result is one row per sample: the called `class`, a probability per
subtype, and a `confidence` column (the max class probability).

## How well did it transfer?

Compare the inferred subtype to CMScaller's reference call:

```{r eval-block, eval = have_deps}
ref <- pData(eset)$cms_pam_all
ok  <- !is.na(ref)

mean(as.character(res$class)[ok] == ref[ok])          # overall agreement
table(reference = ref[ok], inferpheno = res$class[ok]) # per-subtype
```

```{r eval-show, echo = FALSE, eval = !have_deps}
cat("#> [1] 0.6474576\n\n",
    "#>          inferpheno\n",
    "#> reference CMS1 CMS2 CMS3 CMS4\n",
    "#>      CMS1   25    0    0    4\n",
    "#>      CMS2    7   98    9   21\n",
    "#>      CMS3    7    4    4    3\n",
    "#>      CMS4   12   31    6   64\n",
    sep = "")
```

## Visualizing the transfer

The confusion table reads more clearly as a heatmap: cells hold the sample
counts, shaded by per-reference-subtype recall (each row sums to 100%), so a
strong diagonal means faithful transfer.

```{r cm-heatmap, eval = have_plot, fig.width = 5.2, fig.height = 4.4, fig.align = "center"}
library(ggplot2)

ref  <- pData(eset)$cms_pam_all
ok   <- !is.na(ref)
lv   <- c("CMS1", "CMS2", "CMS3", "CMS4")
pred <- factor(as.character(res$class)[ok], levels = lv)
ref  <- factor(ref[ok], levels = lv)

cm        <- table(reference = ref, inferred = pred)
cm_df     <- as.data.frame(cm)
cm_df$recall <- as.data.frame(prop.table(cm, margin = 1))$Freq

ggplot(cm_df, aes(inferred, reference, fill = recall)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "grey90") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 4.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#2166ac",
                      limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Inferred subtype", y = "Reference (CMScaller)", fill = "Row %",
       title = "CMS transfer to held-out metastatic CRC") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

The diagonal holds for CMS1 (86%) and CMS2 (73%); CMS4 is recovered only
moderately (57%, with much of the remainder pulled into CMS2), and CMS3
(bottom row, 22%) scatters — the expected weak spot for the rarest, least
separable subtype.

The `confidence` column — the max class probability — is also informative:
calls that agree with the reference are made far more confidently than the
ones that miss, so confidence is a usable triage signal on a new cohort.

```{r conf-box, eval = have_plot, fig.width = 4.8, fig.height = 4.2, fig.align = "center"}
conf_df <- data.frame(
  confidence = res$confidence[ok],
  outcome    = ifelse(as.character(pred) == as.character(ref),
                      "agrees", "differs"))

ggplot(conf_df, aes(outcome, confidence, fill = outcome)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.55, colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, size = 1, alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(agrees = "#1b7837", differs = "#b2182b")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Confidence (max class probability)",
       title = "Agreeing calls are made more confidently") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

**65% agreement** on a cohort the head never saw — from a panel of just
**three RAVs** (`RAV205`, `RAV476`, `RAV939`), and despite only ~900 of the
basis's ~14,000 genes overlapping this trimmed series, so the projection
degrades gracefully under heavy gene drop-out. CMS1 and CMS2 transfer cleanly;
CMS4 is recovered moderately and CMS3 stays the weak spot. This three-RAV panel
is the size the head ships with: it is the smallest panel that the model
selection rule certifies on a *proper score plus calibration and selection
stability*, deliberately preferred over a larger panel that scores higher on
raw discrimination but overfits and miscalibrates. A larger panel or a
fuller-transcriptome cohort lifts raw agreement, at the cost of the calibration
this compact panel buys.

# Notes for your own data

- **Project a cohort, not single samples.** Scores are standardized across
  the input matrix, so transfer is best when you pass a reasonably sized,
  comparable batch.
- **Transfer is strongest within the trained tissue domain.** A head learns
  whatever distinguishes the label *in its training tissues*. The
  `cms_subtype` head transfers across CRC platforms and stages; do not
  expect a head to carry to an unrelated tissue where the discriminating
  axis may differ. Validate against a labeled held-out set, as above, before
  trusting a new domain.
- **Inspect the panel.** `listRAVs("cms_subtype")` returns the exact RAV
  columns a head uses; `availablePheno()` reports its out-of-fold metric.
